title: Engineering work habits
learner: Returning engineering learners who can perform basic calculations but need a repeatable way to frame, check and document work.
assumedKnowledge: Basic arithmetic and unit meanings; F06 is linked when conversions need review.

include: Frame the problem and make a useful sketch
Estimate first and carry units through the model
Revise and leave a reproducible work record
exclude: Formal engineering design approval, professional certification, laboratory safety procedures, advanced uncertainty statistics and discipline-specific physical laws beyond supplied simple models.

routes.quick: Use four short scenario judgments to locate a gap, read Quick recall, then create a fresh independently completed practical record for each lesson.
routes.full: Build a problem frame, estimate with units, audit results, then revise and communicate. Use guided reviews as needed and retain their assistance label.

overlap: F06 already assesses unit conversions, precision and measurement mathematically; F11 applies them inside a work record.
F03 and F10 supply model and debugging language; this refresher focuses on an auditable process.
reuse.implementation: Reuse QuestionFields and grading for unscored diagnostic judgments only, MathText, page/lesson styles, confidence and plan APIs, useStudyDraft and saveProgress, notes and existing backup. No changes to persistence, backup schema or numerical evidence.

diagnostic.prompt: A page says 12, 3 and 4 beside an unlabeled box. What should you do before choosing an equation?
options: Name the quantities, units, boundary and unknown
Labels connect the picture to a physical model.
Arithmetic cannot supply missing meanings or a requested output.
Visual detail does not replace useful labels.

diagnostic.prompt: You want travel time from 12 km and 4 km/h. Which relationship has the right meaning and units?
options: km divided by km/h gives hours.
That has units km²/h, not time.

diagnostic.prompt: A storage calculation has units of bytes but forgot the number of channels. What does the unit check establish?
options: It checks dimensions but does not prove the value
A missing dimensionless channel count can preserve units and change the result.
Correct units alone do not establish numerical or model correctness.
The answer must have the wrong dimensions
The omitted factor is dimensionless, so this claim is too strong.

diagnostic.prompt: Your corrected answer differs from yesterday's. What makes the revision useful to a future reader?
options: Keep the earlier claim and explain the corrected step and checks
A revision log preserves the reason for the change.
Erase the earlier result and keep only the new number
That hides what changed and why the new result is more trustworthy.
Write that you are now very confident
Confidence is not a record of evidence or method.

assessment.practical: Each objective has a generated fresh scenario, four substantive artifact fields and three explicit self-check criteria. Completion requires saved work, all rubric acknowledgments and a completion timestamp. The app validates presence, not semantic correctness.
assessment.assistance: Revealing a possible review irreversibly marks the active task assisted. A new task has a new seed; the prior completed artifact is retained. Confidence and page visits create no practical evidence.
assessment.evidence: Draft, assisted task recorded, or independent task recorded (self-checked). No percentage, numerical mastery, numerical evidence record, university credit or eligibility claim.

sharedCapabilities.interface: Scoped PracticalLesson and PracticalPath schemas; practical catalog alongside assessed lesson catalog. Course and lesson routes dispatch to practical views before existing readers.
sharedCapabilities.reason: The existing Lesson contract requires four numerical checkpoint questions. Creating dummy questions would misrepresent practical evidence.
sharedCapabilities.integration: Reuse existing visual components/styles and APIs. Add only two route dispatches and availability registration; keep assessed readers, grading and storage contracts unchanged.

sharedCapabilities.interface: learning.notes[courseId]['practical-'+lessonId] stores a versioned JSON envelope with active work and last completed work, each with seed, fields, rubric flags, assistance and completion time.
sharedCapabilities.integration: Each field is at most 400 characters, at most four fields; serialize within the existing 5000-character limit. Ordinary lesson and course notes remain separate. Compare the stored string on save to prevent stale overwrites. Unsupported/corrupt versions remain preserved until deliberately replaced.

sharedCapabilities.interface: learning.notes[courseId]['practical-diagnostic'] stores a small versioned response record.
sharedCapabilities.integration: Show individual feedback and linked review destinations without a total score. This never writes learning.evidence or course completion.

verification: Validate every original calculation and all travel/buffer/fill generators with independent dimensional and arithmetic oracles across 100 seeds; test zero/invalid model inputs at utility boundaries.
Validate strict practical-content and record schemas, 5000-character note limit, version mismatch, corrupted records, sticky assistance, and retained completed work while a fresh draft is started.
Diagnostic feedback identifies lesson-specific gaps without numerical mastery; confidence, visits and diagnostic never create completion records.

Verify draft save/reload, assisted and independent completion, rubric requirements, last-completed retention, notes, export/reset/import, concurrency/conflict protection, keyboard and desktop/mobile Axe/screenshots.
Run all applicable tests, lint, type checks and build. Label preview only after verification; human review pending. Finish F11 before detailed F12 planning.
